title: NVIDIA and Dassault Systèmes' 25-year partnership: from OpenGL to AI world models
dek: Jensen Huang argues that next-generation design tools will no longer rely on humans writing structured geometric data, but instead on AI understanding physics laws and causal relationships through 'world models'—a step harder than language models.
why: A corporate partnership-style fireside chat with modest information density, but Huang's passages on the distinction between 'world models' and language models, and the scale of AI factories, are worth extracting and listening to separately.
who: Founders, engineers, and enterprise digital transformation leads interested in industrial software, digital twins, and AI in manufacturing.
skip: Opening remarks and partnership history recollections (0:13-2:15) contain minimal information; jump straight to the AI infrastructure discussion.

points.h: Design shifts from structured data to generative computing
points.body: Huang says earlier-generation design software required humans to manually specify every geometric shape and material property—everything was structured representation. Now the entire compute stack is being reinvented as a generative computing model. Because AI is infrastructure for all industries, like water, electricity, and the internet, this drives a new round of industrialization in which every country and society will be AI-driven.

points.h: Life is the hardest world model to build
points.body: Huang argues that understanding life first requires learning 'life's language'—how DNA, proteins, and cells interact. This step doesn't exist in physical design, because physical design begins with human imagination, whereas life existed before humans. Only after learning that language can you translate between different languages: human language and biological language, thereby generating new proteins, chemicals, and materials.

points.h: AI predicts physics like a dog catching a ball, not through simulation
points.body: Huang uses an analogy to explain Physics Nemo: a dog catching a ball in the air isn't performing ballistic physics simulation, but simply predicting where it will land through observation. AI learning to predict physical phenomena uses the same logic—trained on physics laws but not solving equations step-by-step. This makes simulation speed 10,000 times faster.

points.h: A gigawatt-scale AI factory costs $50 billion
points.body: Huang calls the present moment a new industrial revolution, requiring simultaneous scaling of three types of factories: chip fabs, computer factories producing supercomputers, and AI factories. He provides specific figures: a gigawatt-scale AI factory costs approximately $50 billion, and the world is simultaneously building dozens of gigawatt-scale factories—humanity's largest-scale industrial infrastructure project in history.

points.h: Future designers will manage an entire team of AI companions
points.body: In response to whether AI will replace engineers, Huang's answer is reversed: in the future, every Solid Works designer will own a team of AI companions trained by that designer themselves. The number of 'users' using Dassault tools will thus expand from purely biological designers to biological plus AI, and total tool usage will instead grow explosively—not shrink.

points.h: World models must obey physics laws, not language preferences
points.body: Huang distinguishes language models from world models: language models need to understand grammar, vocabulary, taste, and guardrails on what should and shouldn't be said; world models must obey physics laws, understand causality—for instance, that knocking over one domino makes connected ones fall—and understand inertia, friction, gravity, and contact relationships. These cannot be captured by language alone; they must be taught through simulation and abundant examples.

points.h: Your AI companion encodes 33 years of expertise and remains private
points.body: Huang says everyone will eventually have an AI companion that remembers your preferences and encodes your skills and habits. This companion won't reside in the cloud, won't be public, won't be open-source, because it carries personally sensitive accumulated knowledge. He cites his own inbox as an example, noting that it already contains 33 years of his professional experience and judgment—precisely what an AI companion should capture.

terms.def: An AI model that follows physics laws and can understand causality and material behavior, distinct from language models that only process language.
NVIDIA's physics-aware AI simulation framework that trains predictive models based on physics laws, 10,000 times faster than traditional simulation.
Model-based systems engineering; an engineering methodology using virtual models to design, simulate, and verify entire systems before construction.
